messages:
sre-bot: Pager — P2: partial egress failure observed in eu-west-2. Multiple customer API timeouts, ~30% of outbound connections hitting errors. Auto-escalating to on-call. https://redwood.internal/incidents/2876543210
sre-bot: Symptoms: 5xx from customer-facing proxies, internal healthchecks showing occasional NAT timeouts, increased TCP RSTs from a subset of NAT IPs.
maya (on-call): I'm on it. Can someone post recent terraform/route changes to eu-west-2 in the last hour?
henri (netops): I see a route propagation batch that finished ~35m ago. Also a queued NAT gateway replacement for AZ-b. Checking NAT gateway health now.
arnav: Confirming customer-facing graph shows spike in upstream 5xx from eu-west-2 -> egress zone. Marking impact: Partial (some customers, degraded throughput).
leo: I can hit service from inside a private subnet via NAT in AZ-b and get timeouts on large downloads (TLS handshake stalls). Small requests succeed.
henri (netops): NAT health checks are flapping on 2 ENIs for nat-azb-gw-03. Metrics: high ErrRate on connections >1MB. Opening CloudTrail/ENI logs.
olivia (prod-eng): Any recent changes to NACLs or SGs? We had a deploy to add an egress allow for caching last night.
arnav: Terraform apply for route_table-assoc happened 52m ago (rollout bot triggered). But there was also a manual quick-change to a route table for a test VPC at +40m, could be noisy.
maya (on-call): Ok, runbook step 1: remove recently associated route table from problematic private subnets to force use of fallback route. Can someone annotate which subnets are on the new association?
henri (netops): Listing assoc now — looks like private-subnet-eu-west-2b and -2c were re-associated. I'll detach assoc and reattach previous table to both. Doing one AZ at a time.
deploy-bot: Terraform plan detected drift for module.vpc.route_table_assoc (manual drift).
henri (netops): Detached assoc from eu-west-2b, reattached previous table. Monitoring.
leo: After 2b reattach, my large download test succeeded in that AZ. Throughput restored in 2b.
maya (on-call): Great — that's promising. Hold on doing 2c until we confirm customers stabilize. Notify support for customers on 2b.
support-bot: Notifying affected customers in eu-west-2b: ticket batch #EW2-443 sent to impacted orgs with temporary mitigation note.
henri (netops): Starting 2c now. Also seeing NAT gateway CPU on nat-azc-gw-05 climb when large flows hit it. Might be a kernel bug with conntrack on big flows.
arnav: If NAT gateways are misbehaving on large flows, fallback plan is to spin up an extra NAT instance in that AZ and shift route to it temporarily.\maya (on-call): Approve create of nat-instance fallback. henri, can you provision a t3.large NAT instance and update route table to point to instance target?
henri (netops): Provisioning — will use AMI patched for conntrack limits. Command: ```aws ec2 run-instances --image-id ami-0fpatched --instance-type t3.large --subnet-id subnet-xxxx --associate-public-ip-address```
henri (netops): Instance up, configuring iptables for MASQUERADE and higher conntrack: ```sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144``` then save.
henri (netops): Updated private-subnet-eu-west-2c route to nat-instance-id i-0fallback. Monitoring connectivity.
leo: Tests from an internal runner in 2c show stable large transfers now.
olivia (prod-eng): Rollback note: we'll revert the manual route_table-assoc change and mark it as root-cause candidate. Anyone who touched the change?
arnav: Manual change was from infra-dev to investigate a test path, not intended for prod. We'll add stricter guardrails.
maya (on-call): Triage summary so far: impact limited to eu-west-2 private subnets in 2b/2c; customers saw intermittent 5xx/timeouts primarily for large outbound flows. Mitigations: reattached prior route table in 2b, spun up NAT instance+route switch in 2c. System load looks stable.
support-bot: Updated tickets: EW2-443 -> mitigation applied, EW2-444 -> follow-up scheduled.
olivia (prod-eng): Postmortem action: enforce terraform-only route_table associations in CI; add automated test for route drift in eu regions. Also consider NAT instance fallback automation.
arnav: Will schedule rollback of manual change and create an RFC for stricter IAM on route changes.
maya (on-call): Closing page: keep monitoring for 30m, then hand off to day SREs. If anything flaps, reopen the thread. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
sre-bot: Incident status: mitigated. Recording timeline and participants. Reference runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/nat-egress-failover
